software.name: SAS/CONNECT
software.description: The code uses RSUBMIT/ENDRSUBMIT remote processing, but no remote host/session configuration or SAS/CONNECT availability is established. PROC SQL and PROC SORT alone do not establish SAS/STAT use.

issues.description: The supplied SAS attachment is substantive partial preparation/merge code, but it has an empty DATA ; SET ; block, a missing keep-list, placeholder input/output table names and no explicit producer for the control-variable table consumed by the final join. The second RSUBMIT block’s remote-session closure and execution order are not shown. Do not treat the attachment as a complete executable driver.

Form 5471 data and IRS-only variable programs are required by the documented workflow but are not in this public package. The cited restrictions are historical limits on publication and IRS-approved access; they do not establish this user’s current grant, retention, eligibility or an automatic current access barrier. Exact IRS fields, schemas and producers remain unresolved.

Country mapping.xlsx is supplied and readable, but no supplied program reads it or identifies how its IRS_COUNTRY_NAME/EX21_COUNTRY_NAME/Country_Name_Final columns feed the withheld IRS merge. The SAS attachment separately creates country_name_final_ex21 using inline Exhibit 21 normalization; the join between those keys is unspecified.

A CRSP.COMPHIST read and GVKEY/date-valid historical CIK/EIN join are supplied in RSUBMIT SQL, and the notes specify an earliest-available historical fallback. The input/output dataset names, compatible current history and coverage, concrete fallback implementation, and producer of the control-variable table consumed by the Exhibit 21 final join remain unresolved. The notes also specify Exhibit 21 EIN fill-in and a conditional EIN-header fallback if EIN remains unavailable; the exact source contract and precedence need clarification. The author defines atm1 as prior-year assets while the raw Compustat query begins at fyear 1990; whether fyear 1990 is analyzed and where prior-year history is retained are unknown. Missing-SIC backfill/forward-fill periods are unspecified.

The supplied merger/acquisition block consumes sale_fn and comments that it comes from comp.funda_fncd, but the function-code file is not read, the frozen catalog query has no exact match, and no join key or producer is supplied. COMP.FUNDA’s readable schema does not establish that this field is there. The separate missing comment terminator and its minimal source repair are recorded under I_SALE_FNCD_COMMENT.

The required I/B/E/S numest merge, RavenPack number_of_articles firm-year input and Audit Analytics comment-letter/restatement firm-year variables lack complete source-to-analysis handoffs. The local catalog provides candidates and bounded probes, but exact product choices, identifier/date crosswalks, annual construction and historical coverage are not all verified. Readable common resources are not treated as independently unlicensed.

The code requires RSUBMIT processing. The environment probe did not establish a working SAS session because TKELS failed to initialize, and no SAS/CONNECT remote session details are included. Component availability remains unverified, not blocked.

At source line 103, the asterisk statement comment has no terminating semicolon. Under SAS comment syntax, it continues through the first semicolon on line 104, swallowing the first sale_fn IF statement and leaving the following ELSE IF unmatched. A single semicolon after the comment text is a supported minimal repair. This repairs the statement boundary only; the sale_fn raw producer and join contract remain unresolved under I_SALE_FNCD.

evidence.quote:
The data sources for the primary analyses are as follows. We downloaded the firm-level non-IRS
data from public sources (Compustat, I/B/E/S, RavenPack, and Audit Analytics) via WRDS as
follows: Compustat data (code run for main set of control variables on September 26, 2018,
updated from original ~August 16, 2017; December 17, 2018 for auditor data), I/B/E/S data
(December 17, 2018), SEC comment letter data (Audit Analytics—November 15, 2017; non-
GAAP SEC comment letters ~July 19, 2019), and RavenPack data (~August 10, 2017). We
obtained Political Risk Index data from Political Risk Services
(https://www.prsgroup.com/category/risk-index, ~August 17, 2017). The Exhibit 21 data are
publicly available here: https://sites.google.com/site/scottdyreng/Home/data-and-code. We use
the file “country31june2019”, assembled on June 25, 2019. Additional information on the
Exhibit 21 data are available at the download site. The confidential corporate tax data comes
from the IRS (see Item #3 for more detail).

In the study, we use unique confidential tax return data filed with the U.S. Internal Revenue

some part of the course of this project Jeff Hoopes and Jaron Wilde were IRS employees under

and for publication in an academic journal. However, the IRS does not allow us to provide the
confidential data or code using IRS dataset names. The IRS supervisor and contact overseeing
this and related work is John Guyton of the IRS (john.guyton@irs.gov).

actions.description: Close the partial preparation and identifier handoffs using author-specified source contracts. Preserve the supplied country mapping and the author-prepared Exhibit 21 route. Do not guess table names, field aliases, period extensions or missing SAS source.
steps: Complete the driver with a compatible implementation once the author field, history and construction contracts are known: fill the COMP.FUNDA keep list, complete the DATA ; SET ; stage, name the input/output tables and specify each producer-consumer handoff, including the second RSUBMIT block.

Use the supplied CRSP.COMPHIST date-valid join once its placeholder input/output names and compatible history coverage are resolved. Preserve the stated earliest-available historical-ID rule. Apply the author-specified Exhibit 21 EIN fill-in and consider the EIN-header source only as a conditional fallback for records still lacking EIN after those steps, with its source contract and precedence confirmed. Produce historical IDs and the control-variable table before the Exhibit 21 final consumer.
Resolve the source and join keys for sale_fn from the author-noted comp.funda_fncd product; do not infer sale_fn from the readable COMP.FUNDA table.

Preserve Country mapping.xlsx as the supplied lookup. Confirm whether it is manually applied or imported, its relationship to the inline country_name_final_ex21 normalization, and the exact key passed into the IRS merge.

If the study workflow uses the cited Exhibit 21 file, use the prepared country31june2019 input and verify its actual fields before running the supplied country normalization. Clarify where atm1 is produced and whether an observation at fyear 1990 is part of the analysis; if it is, supply the preceding fiscal-year at input needed for that observation.
